question: m09
q: Have building approvals picked up since the RBA started cutting?

transcript.answer:
**Yes, approvals are higher than before the cuts.** The gain came in two stages. Apartments and other medium-density dwellings rose first, and houses followed later. Approvals kept rising after the RBA started raising rates again in 2026.

**Rate path (RBA cash rate, monthly average)**
- The rate was 4.35% through January 2025. Cuts began in February 2025 (4.25% monthly average) and the rate reached 3.60% by September 2025.
- It held at 3.60% until January 2026, then rose to 4.35% by June 2026. It was 4.36% in September 2026.

**Approvals (ABS, dwelling units, Australia)**

I compared March–August each year, using the original series. I couldn't retrieve the seasonally adjusted series, so year-on-year comparisons avoid seasonal distortion. The component totals differ from the headline total by about 20 dwellings, which I'm treating as rounding.

| Mar–Aug total | 2024 (pre-cuts) | 2025 | 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total residential | 86,739 | 97,407 (+12.3%) | 108,303 (+11.2%) |
| Houses | 57,770 | 57,966 (+0.3%) | 67,037 (+15.7%) |
| Dwellings excluding houses | 28,989 | 39,469 (+36%) | 41,289 (+4.6%) |

**Latest month**
- August 2026 had 16,967 approvals, up 10.3% on August 2025 (15,377).
- That was down from 19,273 in July 2026. Monthly original data is volatile, so I wouldn't read much into one month.
- Houses were 11,134 in August 2026, against 9,730 in August 2025.

**Caveats**
- Approvals have risen, but I can't show the cuts caused it. Approvals often lag rate changes, and supply policy and construction costs also matter.
- The 2026 gains came while rates were rising again. That suggests the response to the 2025 cuts was still flowing through, or other factors are at work.
